solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Tom possibly injured Paul with tip of this weapon

parts.note: a tom is a male cat, so cat is an example of what a tom may be

indicators.note: something injured is knocked out of shape, so the name beside it is rearranged

parts.note: the man's name taken as written, before rearranging

indicators.note: the tip of a word is its leading letter, so only the start of the following word is kept

parts.note: the opening letter of this

explanation.surface: A tomcat hurts a man called Paul with the point of some weapon.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tom' reads as a man's name alongside Paul, but here it is the male cat.
explanation.definitionFit: A catapult is a hand-held or siege device for hurling stones, so it counts as a weapon.

clue.text: Arresting type gathering last of bumper yield

indicators.note: gathering means taking something in, so the first word surrounds the letter that follows

parts.note: a cop is a police officer, someone who arrests people

indicators.note: last of asks for the final letter of the next word only

parts.note: the final letter of bumper

explanation.surface: A police officer takes in a record harvest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Arresting' looks like 'striking', describing a type, but it means making arrests.
explanation.definitionFit: A crop is the amount of produce a field gives in one season, its harvest or yield.

clue.text: Person taking holiday just before the fall?

definitions.text: Person taking holiday just before the fall?

parts.words: Person taking holiday just before the fall?
parts.note: surface reading: someone going away on a trip at the end of summer, before autumn
setter's reading: someone who stumbles is doing so the instant before tumbling over; the word also means a day visitor

explanation.walkthrough: 'The fall' is the American word for autumn, which makes the clue look like a late-summer holiday; it is also a literal tumble.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both a sightseer on a short excursion and, literally, one who stumbles over something.

clue.text: Very old priest involved with choir

indicators.note: involved means tangled up, so the letters of the two words are mixed together

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: An elderly clergyman takes part in the church singers' activities.
explanation.definitionFit: Something from before written records is ancient, hence used loosely for anything extremely old-fashioned.

clue.text: Up-to-date news from the French trial

parts.note: la is a French word for the, feminine form
a test is a trial or examination

explanation.surface: The most recent bulletin arrives from a court case in France.
explanation.definitionFit: "Have you heard the latest?" uses the word as a noun meaning the most recent information or developments.

clue.text: Almost perfect notion

indicators.note: almost means not quite all, so the word that follows loses its final letter

parts.note: ideal means perfect, flawless

explanation.surface: A thought that is very nearly flawless.
explanation.definitionFit: A notion is a thought or concept formed in the mind, the same thing as this word.

clue.text: Indian loincloth some remained hot in

indicators.note: some means only part of what follows, so the answer sits inside the run of words

parts.note: found across the end of remained, all of hot and the word in

explanation.surface: Someone stayed in a light Indian garment because the weather was hot.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the length of cloth wrapped around the waist and legs traditionally worn by men in India.

clue.text: US soldier in car or rising aircraft

indicators.note: in a down clue rising means read from the bottom upwards, so the word or is turned around
in places the soldier inside the letters that come from the other words

parts.note: auto is short for automobile, a car
taken as written
GI is the standard term for an American soldier

explanation.surface: An American soldier sits in a car or takes off in a flying machine.
explanation.definitionFit: This is an early rotorcraft whose unpowered rotor spins freely while a propeller drives it forward, a type of light aircraft.

clue.text: Piece of fruit — round, as it happens

parts.note: the letter O is round in shape
a live broadcast is shown as it happens

explanation.surface: A small fruit turns out, as it happens, to be round.
explanation.walkthrough: 'As it happens' looks like a throwaway phrase meaning 'by chance', but it means broadcast in real time.
explanation.definitionFit: An olive is a single small stone fruit of the Mediterranean tree, so one counts as a piece of fruit.

clue.text: Trade union golf club keeping old towing vessel

indicators.note: keeping means holding on to, so the club holds the next letter inside it

parts.note: TU is the abbreviation for trade union
golf is G in the NATO phonetic alphabet
a bat is a club used to strike a ball
O is the abbreviation for old

explanation.surface: A union and a golf club have kept an antique boat used for towing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Golf club' reads as a single thing, but golf and club give separate pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: A tugboat is a small powerful boat that pulls or pushes larger ships, a towing vessel.

clue.text: Sombre Aussie soldier, one working in churchyard

parts.note: grave means serious or sombre
digger is slang for an Australian or New Zealand soldier

explanation.surface: A gloomy Australian soldier now has a job in a churchyard.
explanation.definitionFit: A gravedigger is employed to excavate burial plots, so is a worker found in a churchyard or cemetery.

clue.text: Conscientious way a top man accompanies father home

indicators.note: accompanies means goes alongside, so these pieces are placed next to the others

parts.note: pa is an informal word for father
in means at home
ST is the abbreviation for street, a way
taken as written
a king is the man at the top of a kingdom

explanation.surface: A dutiful way for a ruler to go with his father as he heads home.
explanation.walkthrough: The pieces are given in a different order from the clue: the father and home come first, then the way and the top man.
explanation.definitionFit: Painstaking work is done with great care and thoroughness, which is what conscientious describes.

clue.text: Feud involving archdeacon and one owing money, we hear

parts.note: Ven, for Venerable, is the title used for an archdeacon

indicators.note: we hear means the words are to be taken as they sound when spoken

parts.note: a debtor owes money; spoken in a non-rhotic accent it sounds like detta

explanation.surface: A quarrel involving a senior clergyman and someone in debt.
explanation.walkthrough: In British speech the final R of debtor is silent and the B is never pronounced, so it sounds like detta.
explanation.definitionFit: A vendetta is a prolonged bitter quarrel or blood feud between families or people.

clue.text: Mistakes encountered in Canberra talks

indicators.note: encountered in says the answer is met lying inside the following words

parts.note: found across the end of Canberra and the start of talks

explanation.surface: Errors made during diplomatic negotiations in Australia's capital.
explanation.definitionFit: Errata are printing or writing errors, especially those listed as corrections in a book, so the plural of erratum.

clue.text: Church caretaker, initially rather on edge

indicators.note: in an across clue on means placed after, so this letter follows the other piece

parts.note: a verge is an edge or border

indicators.note: initially points to the first letter of the word next to it

parts.note: the opening letter of rather

explanation.surface: A church caretaker who is, from the start, somewhat nervous.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On edge' looks like a phrase meaning nervous, but on and edge do separate jobs.
explanation.definitionFit: A verger is an official who looks after the interior of a church and acts as attendant at services.

clue.text: Italian citizens — small number feeding web-footed birds

indicators.note: feeding means being put into, so the number goes inside the birds

parts.note: geese are web-footed waterfowl
no is the short form of number

explanation.surface: People from an Italian city are giving food to a few ducks or geese.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Small' means the abbreviation of number, not a few. Genoa is a port city in north-west Italy.
explanation.definitionFit: Genoese is the collective term for the people of Genoa, so they are citizens of an Italian city.

clue.text: Sign of injury on a black beetle

indicators.note: in a down clue on means placed above, so the first piece sits over the rest

parts.note: a scar is a mark left by an injury
taken as written
B is the abbreviation for black, as on pencils

explanation.surface: A wound mark appears on a dark-coloured beetle.
explanation.definitionFit: The scarab is a dung beetle held sacred in ancient Egypt, so it is a kind of beetle.

clue.text: Girl's pulling power, a diversion

parts.note: Di is a short girl's name; with the apostrophe S it becomes possessive
traction is the power of pulling a load

explanation.surface: A young woman's attractiveness serves to draw attention away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pulling power' looks like charm or sex appeal, but it is literal hauling force.
explanation.definitionFit: A distraction is something that draws attention away from what one should be doing, the same as a diversion.

clue.text: When speaking, remained sober

indicators.note: when speaking means the word is judged by how it is said out loud

parts.note: stayed means remained, and it is pronounced identically

explanation.surface: Someone stayed sober while talking.
explanation.definitionFit: Staid describes a serious, sedate, unadventurous manner, which is the sense of sober meaning restrained.

clue.text: Astonish tabloid, seizing end of report

indicators.note: seizing means grabbing hold, so the newspaper wraps around the letter

parts.note: The Sun is a British tabloid newspaper

indicators.note: end of asks for only the final letter of the word after it

parts.note: the final letter of report

explanation.surface: A newspaper amazes readers by grabbing the conclusion of a story.
explanation.definitionFit: To stun someone is to shock or amaze them so they are stupefied, the same as to astonish.

clue.text: 1100 on returning craft, a river passenger transport

indicators.note: in an across clue on means placed after, so the number follows the turned word
returning means going back, so the word craft is read backwards

parts.note: art is a craft or skill
1100 in Roman numerals is M (1000) plus C (100)
taken as written
R is the abbreviation for river

explanation.surface: Eleven hundred boats come back, a river vessel carrying passengers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Craft' suggests a boat but means skill.
explanation.definitionFit: A tramcar is a single vehicle of a street tramway, which carries passengers along rails.

clue.text: Blast of wind engulfing European visitor

indicators.note: engulfing means swallowing up, so the blast surrounds the letter for European

parts.note: a gust is a sudden blast of wind
E is the abbreviation for European

explanation.surface: A sudden wind sweeps over a visitor from Europe.
explanation.definitionFit: A guest is someone invited to stay at a home or hotel, a person who is visiting.

clue.text: Practical Cockney chap

indicators.note: Cockneys, Londoners of the East End, famously drop the H sound at the start of words

parts.note: handy means practical or useful

explanation.surface: A useful London man.
explanation.walkthrough: The Cockney accent is the working-class East London one, which drops initial H.
explanation.definitionFit: Andy is a common man's name, and crosswords freely use any male name for chap.

clue.text: Scottish city woman in a Swiss city

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: in means placed inside, so the woman goes within the city's name

parts.note: Bern is the Swiss capital
Dee is a woman's name

explanation.surface: A woman from a Scottish city visits a city in Switzerland.
explanation.definitionFit: Aberdeen is the granite city on Scotland's north-east coast, the country's third largest.
